description:
Real Time Transcoding buffers outside LAN with QSV

I'm very excited for HLS support in Immich but I think there's something up with how it handles streaming with lower bandwidth or higher latency. On my LAN I probably have ~600 mbit connection from my laptop here to my server and the playback is pretty flawless, but if I change my DNS to test streaming over my 40 megabit WAN link there is a stutter every couple of seconds where it buffers. I'm using qsv with an Intel Arc A770 and I can see in the logs `Session _ lead is _ segments`, and that lead number rises so it's able to transcode quicker than I'm watching. The `encoded-video` directory is over a nfs share on HDDs but since playback works over LAN, I don't think that is the issue either. Jellyfin and Frigate are 2 other "video" apps I expose and I am able to playback just fine through…

notes: Symptom-only user report (QSV real-time HLS buffering outside LAN); fix adds -b:v for non-CQP QSV in QsvSwDecodeConfig.getBitrateOptions; RC exact. Symptom-to-fix distance is large (needs FFmpeg knowledge) but the patch comment cites issue #29220, so mapping is right.

indirect_boundary label "job" is wrong: the reported path is the real-time HLS route (VideoStreamController -> HlsService.serverSend HlsSegmentRequest/HlsSessionRequest -> TranscodingService @OnEvent handler -> BaseConfig.create/getCommand -> ffmpeg), i.e. cross-worker server events, not a BullMQ job. Correct to "event".

tests: media.service.spec.ts: MediaService handleVideoConversion should set options for qsv with sw decode
